newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes lower after record delivery.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes lower after record delivery.

text.p: IPE gas oil ended on Tuesday slightly lower after the November contract expiry produced a record 865,100 tonnes delivery into open positions, brokers said.

December gas oil closed 75 cents lower at $211.00 per tonne when December Brent stood at $22.83, 18 cents down on the day. When November gas oil expired at $220.00 per tonne, the Nov/Dec spread stood at $8.50 backwardation.
"There was not much changing of positions before the close today," a broker said, though he thought the major long into expiry sold 2,000 November contracts at $9 backwardation Monday.

November's expiry produced 856,100 tonnes of heating oil to be delivered in ARA in the second half of November, principally by one trading company to one other. "Some of it will probably go to the Far East," the broker added.
Increasing the downwards pressure on gas oil was news that European stocks rose sharply last month.

Euroilstock Foundation said middle distillate stocks in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose 6.60 million barrels in October, trimming the year-on-year shortfall to 21.65 million barrels or 6.9 percent. By 1807 GMT, December Brent stood 24 cents lower at $22.77 per barrel.

Dealers said crude could be resuming a technical downtrend which began last month. They said the market was vulnerable to further weakness, given a break through technical support at $22.80 and depressed physical markets.
Also, December North Sea loading programmes, due to be released later this week, are expected to schedule bigger volumes than in November, traders said.
